title: Atomic‐Scale Insights Into the Thermal Stability of High‐Entropy Nanoalloys

recollection.starting_material: guess: computational models of high‐entropy alloy nanoparticles, probably equiatomic mixtures of 5–6 transition metals such as Co–Cr–Fe–Ni–Cu
recollection.intervention: guess: large-scale ab-initio molecular dynamics or machine-learning–accelerated Monte Carlo simulations were performed while heating the nanoalloys to various temperatures
recollection.structure: guess: observation of elemental segregation patterns versus retained random solid-solution character as particle size changes (e.g., 2–5 nm FCC nanocrystals)
recollection.mechanism: guess: competition between configurational entropy that favors mixing and surface/strain energies that drive segregation; surface depletion/enrichment of specific elements explained by relative surface energies and atomic size mismatch
recollection.results: guess: identified a critical particle diameter (~4 nm) and temperature (~800 K) above which significant surface segregation of Cu and Cr occurs, while Co, Fe, Ni remain mixed in the core; calculated activation energies for elemental diffusion of 0.6–1.2 eV and showed that thermal stability (random mixing) is enhanced by ~30 % compared with binary alloys

score.note: The recollection only generically captures heating/simulation and partially anticipates segregation in FCC nanoparticles. It correctly identifies surface-energy-driven elemental segregation as a key mechanism, but incorrectly emphasizes entropy/strain competition and misses the kinetically controlled, non-sluggish diffusion and reshaping effects. The stated composition, methods, critical size, temperature, activation energies, and stability enhancement are wrong; it also misses the observed 22% size reduction at 973 K.
